why: A runs one editorial system end to end — numbered section markers (01-08) in a mono face, alternating pale and blue bands, a single left-aligned type scale — and its copy names things only an operator knows (TR TS 021/2011, ATP body classes, FRC for frozen, thermograph readings, veterinary and phytosanitary control at the border), so the page argues rather than advertises. B's first screen is broken: the Russian/Kazakh/English switcher sits on top of the hero headline and swallows the first line, which is the one piece of text everything else depends on. B then repeats the same primary CTA twice within a screen, uses the identical snowflake icon for both 'Chilled products' and 'Frozen cargo', and fills six route cards with the same shell and a large pocket of dead space where content should be.
loser_fatal_flaw: The language switcher overlaps and occludes the hero headline, so the page's opening sentence is unreadable at the very top of the page.
winner_worst_flaw: Its social proof is fake: the client 'logos' are just company names typeset in the page's own font inside plain boxes, with the fifth one orphaned and centred under a two-column grid — a wall of placeholders standing in for evidence on a page whose whole argument is evidence.
ai_evidence: Headline built as a two-fragment couplet, 'Your route. Our solution.', with the second line recoloured — the standard generated-landing device
Copy that says nothing checkable: 'Tell us what you are shipping and we will discuss a suitable option', 'We match the refrigerated truck to your product'
The same snowflake glyph used for two different cargo categories, each in the identical rounded tinted icon square
Six route cards that are one card repeated, with a large empty gap between the route name and the link because every card is padded to a fixed shell
Route labels that overlap in meaning rather than partition the map: Kazakhstan-Europe, Europe-CIS, CIS countries-Kazakhstan
The canonical three-question FAQ (what does it cost / can you do it urgently / how is it monitored) with every answer collapsed
A visible 'Skip to content' box rendered at the top of the capture
